newsitem.title: USA: US CASH GRADES SLIP LOWER IN GULF, WTS LEADS MOVE.
newsitem.headline: US CASH GRADES SLIP LOWER IN GULF, WTS LEADS MOVE.

text.p: Cash crude grade prices in the U.S. Gulf slipped lower Thursday morning, led by a softening for West Texas Sour/Midland barrels, traders said.
Outright benchmark September WTI/Cushing pulled back to unchanged from Wednesday, talked currently around flat at $20.45-55 a barrel.
Grade business featured WTS/Midland selling at a $1.51 discount to the marker, down a shade from deals Wednesday between $1.48 to $1.50 under September WTI.
Traders said Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James moved at a 14 cents premium to WTI, down four cents from late deals recorded on Wednesday.
Soft Brent values and expectations for deliveries to the U.S. Gulf have worked against LLS, traders said.
Other numbers out in the market had Postings Plus for September at $1.88-90, relfecting a widening in the September/October roll out to minus 13 cents.
Midland/WTI weakened slightly to a 32-29 cents discount, in-line with the LLS retreat.
Moves by Iraq were again at the forefront of market conversation, notably reports both BP and Shell were declined in their bids to renew oil contracts for the second round of the "oil-for-food" deal.
One trader said he was surprised by the move, and emphasized that the Iraqis appeared to be politics with oil contract awards.
"They've said they would favor companies and countries who have helped their cause in the past, so this looks like it is part of that," said a crude dealer.
Other companies, such as France's Elf, said they expected to receive new Iraqi contracts.

Final approval for implementing the accord is seen Friday morning, after a 48-hour "no-objection" procedure expires under Sanctions Committee rules. Iraq would then be free to submit oil contracts to U.N. overseers from Friday.
